Die Suchergebnisse zeigen die KBA-Zahlen für das erste Halbjahr 2026, allerdings über Sekundärquellen. Eine offizielle KBA-Pressemitteilung war nicht darunter.

**Halbjahr 2026 (Januar bis Juni):**
- Insgesamt wurden 1.484.393 Pkw neu zugelassen. Davon hatten 966.085 alternative Antriebe, was 65,1 % entspricht. Der Anteil der Neuzulassungen mit alternativen Antrieben am Gesamtzulassungsvolumen von 1.484.393 Pkw erreichte mit 966.085 Neuwagen insgesamt 65,1 Prozent.
- BEV-Neuzulassungen: 368.006 Elektro/BEV-Pkw ... entsprach einem Anteil von 24,8 Prozent am Gesamtzulassungsvolumen und einem Plus von 48,0 Prozent gegenüber dem gleichen Zeitraum des Vorjahres.
- Elektrifizierte Antriebe inklusive Plug-in-Hybriden und Brennstoffzelle kamen auf 531.808 Neuzulassungen und einen Anteil von 35,8 %, was im Vergleich zum Vorjahreszeitraum einem Anstieg von 37,2 Prozent entsprach.

**Juni 2026 (Monat):**
- Im Juni wurden laut dem Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA) in Deutschland 296.378 Personenkraftwagen neu zugelassen., was ein Plus von 15,7 Prozent gegenüber dem Vorjahresmonat bedeutet.
- Der BEV-Anteil lag laut KBA bei 28,4 %, nach 18,4 % im Juni 2025 (ein Anstieg um zehn Prozentpunkte). Die Zahl von 84.057 Elektro-Pkw bedeutete ein Plus von 78,2 Prozent.
- Mit Plug-in-Hybriden (10,9 %) lagen Stecker-Fahrzeuge im Juni zusammen bei fast 40 % (Rechnet man den 10,9-Prozent-Anteil der Plug-in-Hybride (PHEV) hinzu, waren im Juni fast 40 Prozent aller neu zugelassenen Pkw Fahrzeuge mit Stecker.).

**Einordnung:** Der ZDK hatte für 2026 einen durchschnittlichen BEV-Anteil von 25 % prognostiziert, nach 19,1 % im Jahr 2025 (Der ZDK hatte für 2026 einen durchschnittlichen Anteil von 25 Prozent batterieelektrischer Fahrzeuge (BEV) an allen Pkw-Neuzulassungen prognostiziert).

Hinweis: Die Zahlen stammen aus Berichten von ecomento und mobiflip, die sich auf das KBA berufen. Für Zitate in einer offiziellen Form sollte man die KBA-Pressemitteilung direkt prüfen.

Germany's new EV subsidy is already open for applications. Reports from May 2026 say the portal opened after the Bundesrat approved the scheme. Germany has officially opened applications for its new electric vehicle subsidy scheme after the program cleared its final legislative hurdle with approval from the Bundesrat earlier this month.

**Launch and eligibility dates:** The scheme covers vehicles first registered from 1 January 2026, and applications can be filed retroactively. The scheme applies retroactively to vehicles registered on or after 1 January 2026. Applications require a completed registration. Applications can only be submitted after the vehicle has been registered.

**Amounts:** Battery-electric vehicles get €3,000 to €6,000, and plug-in hybrids and range extenders get €1,500 to €4,500. Buyers of new battery-electric vehicles can receive between €3,000 and €6,000, while plug-in hybrids and range extenders qualify for grants of between €1,500 and €4,500. The top amount requires a taxable household income of €45,000 or less and at least two minor children. Income-based bonuses are €1,000 for households below €60,000 and €2,000 below €45,000. Each child under 18 adds €500, up to €1,000.

**Income limits:** The standard ceiling is €80,000 in taxable household income. For families, the threshold increases: +€5,000 per child (up to two children), up to €90,000 for households with two or more children. Eligibility is based on the average taxable income from the two most recent tax assessments.

**Budget and scope:** The programme has €3 billion through 2029, intended to support about 800,000 vehicles. The program applies exclusively to newly registered vehicles. There is currently no vehicle price cap and no domestic-content requirement linked to production location.

**Discrepancies:** Sources differ on plug-in hybrid rules. One source says PHEV eligibility is limited to between 1 January 2026 and 30 June 2027. Another gives the criteria as emit no more than 60 g CO₂/km (type-approval value) or offer an electric driving range of at least 80 kilometers. A third source cites a 50-mile range requirement instead of 80 km. Check the official portal or ministry guidance before relying on the PHEV details.

The SMMT's January 2026 outlook projects UK new car registrations rising 1.4% to 2.048 million units in 2026, a more optimistic view than its October forecast. With January typically a lower volume month and not necessarily indicative of the full year trend, the body did not treat the slow start as a warning sign.

The BEV forecast is 28.5% of the market. That is above 2025's level but still below the 33% ZEV mandate for 2026. The ZEV mandate target for carmakers in 2026 is 33% of their fleet, up from 28% last year.

The January BEV figures explain the weak start. BEV uptake rose just 0.1% to 29,654 units, a 20.6% market share, the lowest since April 2025. The SMMT attributes this partly to a strong January 2025, when uptake was pulled forward ahead of April's new BEV tax rates. PHEVs were the strongest performers, rising 47.3% to account for 12.9% of registrations.

The SMMT says the forecast improvement reflects increasing model choice, improved range and the re-introduction of government support through the Electric Car Grant. It also warns that the 33% target is still out of reach and calls for a holistic review of the transition, citing the proposed eVED from 2028 as a further drag on demand.

Kelley Blue Book's Q4 2025 numbers show a sharp fourth-quarter drop after a record third quarter, though full-year volume held up. I found no primary Cox or KBB release, so these figures come from secondary summaries.

- **Q4 volume:** One summary puts Q4 sales at 234,000 units, a 46% drop from Q3 and 36% below Q4 2024. It calls that the weakest quarter since Q4 2022 (U.S. EV sales fell sharply in Q4 2025 to 234k units (-46% QoQ, -36% YoY)).
- **Q4 share:** EV share of new-vehicle sales fell to 5.8% in Q4, down from a 10.5% peak in Q3 (EV share of total new-vehicle sales fell to 5.8% in Q4 (from a peak 10.5% in Q3)).
- **Tax credit timing:** The drop is attributed to incentives ending. Buyers pulled purchases forward, and several government-backed sales incentives ending at the start of October contributed to the late-year contraction.
- **Full year:** KBB estimates 2025 sales of just under 1.30 million, about 2% below 2024, making it the second-best year on record (U.S. EV sales in 2025 totaled just under 1.30 million units, a decline of roughly 2% compared to 2024. This made 2025 the second-best year on record for EV sales in the U.S.).
- **Full-year share:** EVs reached 7.8% of new-vehicle sales for 2025, versus 8.1% in 2024 (EV share for all of 2025 came in at 7.8% (vs 8.1% in 2024)).
- **Brands:** Tesla sold 589k EVs in 2025, close to half the market, and GM passed 150k, with about 13% share (Tesla remained the dominant EV seller, with 2025 sales of 589k units (-7% YoY, -44k units); GM reaching roughly 13% of total U.S. EV sales).
- **Outlook:** Cox expects EV share near 8% in 2026, citing a wider model lineup and better charging reliability (Cox Automotive expects EV share to be near 8% in 2026).

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

          Cox Automotive Forecast: New-Vehicle Sales Pace Holds Strong Through First
                Half of 2026 Despite Continued Economic and Policy Uncertainty

          •    The June new-vehicle sales pace is expected to finish near 16.1 million, mostly
               unchanged from the pace in May and up from last June’s pace of 15.8 million.
          •    Sales volume is expected to rise to 1.34 million units, up 4.2% from last year but
               lower by 9.7% compared to May.
          •    GM remains the first-half leader despite, as Toyota gains share and closes the gap.

ATLANTA, June 24, 2026 – The June SAAR is expected to finish near 16.1 million, roughly in line with
March, April and May—an unusual period of consistency given recent volatility and high energy prices.
June sales volume, forecast at 1.34 million units, will show a gain compared to June 2025, but a decline
from May. June has 25 selling days, one more than last year and one less than last month.

With healthy June sales, second-quarter volume is forecast to finish above the weather-impacted first
quarter. Even so, total new-vehicle sales in the first half of 2026 are tracking 3.6% lower year over year.

Despite continued economic and policy uncertainty, the new-vehicle market has proven to be relatively
resilient in 2026. Recent geopolitical tension and higher gas prices have had limited impact on demand,
with shoppers largely holding steady. After a volatile stretch earlier in the year driven by weather and
policy shifts, the monthly sales pace has largely stabilized.

Affordability remains a central constraint, increasingly shaped by broader household finances rather
than vehicle prices alone. Elevated interest rates, higher costs for essentials, and tighter budgets are
limiting purchasing power across income levels. Even so, strong equity markets and accumulated
household wealth are helping support demand. Assuming no major policy shocks, the new-vehicle
market in 2026 is expected to continue fluctuating in the high-15 to low-16 million range. The Cox
Automotive full year forecast remains unchanged at 15.8 million, a decline of 2.9% from 2025.

“Although there is a tremendous amount of economic and policy uncertainty these days, the new-
vehicle market seems to be relatively unfazed. Thus far, vehicle buyers have shrugged off the latest
shock – the Iran War and higher gas prices – as new-vehicle sales have been fairly stable the last few
months,” said Cox Automotive Senior Economist Charlie Chesbrough.

  Mid-Size SUV/Crossover         200,315      253,855         230,000      14.8%   -9.4%    17.3%        17.2%       1.6%
      Other Segments             525,940      584,618         525,000      -0.2%   -10.2%   39.0%        39.3%       -1.7%
        Grand Total            1,280,846     1,478,496       1,335,000     4.2%    -9.7%
Cox Automotive Economic and Industry Insights Estimates
 First Half Sales Lower Compared to 2025
General Motors remains the volume leader through the first half of 2026, but its top spot is under
pressure. The automaker is expected to finish the second quarter with just under 705,000 vehicles sold,
down 5.1% year over year; first-half sales are tracking 7.2% lower. All GM brands are posting declines,
led by Buick and Cadillac, each down more than 20% for the first half, resulting in a modest loss of
market share.

Toyota momentum continues, and the company is emerging as a challenger for the top spot. Second-
quarter sales are expected to rise 18.8% from the first quarter—well ahead of the broader market—
fueled by strong demand for redesigned products and broad hybrid offerings. This growth is helping
Toyota expand, narrowing the gap with GM to less than 100,000 units and setting up a potential shift in
leadership by year-end if trends hold.

Elsewhere, performance across automakers is mixed. Hyundai Motor Group continues to deliver steady
gains, with first-half share increasing by 0.7 percentage points. Stellantis sales have also rebounded,
with volume up 4.8% and market share improving after several years of decline. In contrast, Cox
Automotive sales estimates suggest Ford is facing a challenging year, with first-half sales expected to
fall 10.3%, while Tesla is also under pressure, with volumes down 14.6% amid intensifying competition
and fewer products to sell.

economic headwinds. The full-year new-vehicle sales pace is forecast to be 15.8 million units, a 2.9%

the sales outlook. Inflationary pressures tied to energy costs and ongoing affordability challenges have
weighed on consumer sentiment. Even with elevated interest rates and cautious consumers, the new-
vehicle market has remained resilient.

market in 2026 hasn’t changed in a meaningful way since January,” said Cox Automotive Chief

The December 17, 2025 Cox Automotive forecast called for 2025 full-year sales of 16.3 million, and later Cox updates kept that figure.

- **The original forecast:** The December 17 release said new-vehicle sales would finish 2025 up 1.8% year over year, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates, and a volume of 16.3 million would make 2025 the best sales year since 2019.
- **The December SAAR forecast:** Cox expected the December seasonally adjusted annual rate near 15.9 million, down from last year's 16.8 million pace but up from November's 15.6 million level.
- **The January 2026 update:** Cox's January 7, 2026 update said the December SAAR came in at 16.0 million, near the Cox forecast of 15.9 million. Its January 27, 2026 release described 2025 as ending at an estimated 16.3 million units. It also gave December's SAAR as an upwardly revised 16.1 million.
- **The SAAR nuance:** A Cox note in the December deck said the annual sales pace in 2025 is now forecast at 16.2 million. So 16.3 million is a volume figure based on Kelley Blue Book counts, while the SAAR figure is about 16.2 million.
- **Later confirmation:** A September 2026 Cox presentation lists CY2025: 16.3 million.

content.content:
**June 2026 (CPCA retail, passenger vehicles)**

- **Total passenger vehicle retail:** 1.602 million units, "a sharp 23.2% drop from a year earlier," and up 6.1% from May.
- **NEV retail:** "came in at 1.007 million units in June," down 9.4% year on year. This was the sixth straight annual decline, but the first month of 2026 above 1 million.
- **NEV penetration:** 62.8%. The article says it was "up 9.5 percentage points year-on-year" and 0.1 point below May's record high.
- **BEV vs. PHEV/EREV:** BEV sales reached 685,000, up 3.6% year on year. PHEV sales were 241,000 (down 27.3%), and EREV sales were 82,000 (down 31.9%). The article calls "Battery electric vehicles (BEVs)" the "main pillar of the NEV market."
- **Gasoline vehicles:** Conventional gasoline passenger vehicle retail "plunged 39% year-on-year in June." Pure gasoline fell 42%, and ordinary hybrids fell 7%.
- **Exports (June):** NEV exports "jumped 152.7% year-on-year," reaching 499,000 units and a record 56.9% of passenger vehicle exports. Total passenger vehicle exports were 877,000, up 82.3%.

**H1 2026**

The article does not report H1 totals. These figures are my own sums of the monthly tables, so treat them as estimates:

- **Passenger vehicle retail:** about 8.72 million, down roughly 19.9% from about 10.89 million in H1 2025.
- **NEV retail:** about 4.71 million, down roughly 13.6% from about 5.46 million.
- **NEV share:** about 54%. The article does not give an H1 penetration rate.
- **H1 exports:** not reported.

**Not covered in the article**

- Price war or price cut index
- Purchase tax changes
- Comments on luxury, premium, joint venture, or imported cars
